messages.content: Minneapolis is five days out. Can you sanity-check the plan now that badge pickup moved buildings? I’m booked Sunday late afternoon nonstop, North Loop hotel through Wednesday, Wednesday evening flight home, no car.

The itinerary still works. I would not add a rental car for this change; it would create more parking hassle than benefit. Use rideshare from MSP Sunday night, and give Monday morning a bigger cushion because badge pickup is no longer at the lab building and downtown construction can slow cars.
Badge pickup opens 7:45 in the Phillips building, then the practical lab starts at 9 in Moos Tower. I don’t know if that’s walkable with the weather.

Plan on a rideshare from the hotel around 7:05 Monday. That should cover construction, a badge line, and the building change. After pickup, if it’s raining hard or windy, rideshare the short hop to Moos; if it’s just misting, walk only if the organizer confirms the indoor route or a straightforward campus path.
What about Sunday from the airport? Is light rail worth it to North Loop?

With an evening arrival, light rain, and cold wind, I’d skip the train unless rideshare pricing is absurd. Take a rideshare directly to the hotel, text the hotel if you’re delayed, and keep dinner easy near the hotel rather than walking around looking for something.
Hotel confirmed a room away from elevators and that pool and gym access are open. Hot tub is still out.

That’s good enough to leave the hotel alone. Keep the quiet-room confirmation in the trip notes, and assume the hot tub is unavailable rather than trying to re-shop this close in. Pool or gym after Monday is still useful if the schedule allows.
Both window seats are selected, but the return aircraft says seat map may change. Also remind me what should go in the small work bag.

For seats: screenshot the current outbound and return seats now, check the return seat map again 72 hours out and at check-in, and if the aircraft swaps, choose any free window in the same cabin before paying for an upgrade. Small bag: laptop, charger, phone battery, ID, workshop confirmation, badge-pickup email, one notebook, pen, compact umbrella, rain shell or packable layer, clinic cards, and only the lab materials you need Monday morning. Leave the roller at the hotel after check-in so the badge-to-lab move stays light.

messages.content: I’m back from Minneapolis and need to switch gears. We have a family graduation weekend in Madison in mid-May, two of us. Ceremony is Saturday morning, but the family is still deciding between a Friday dinner and a Sunday brunch.

Got it. I’d treat the family schedule as the thing that drives both flights and hotel area. Are you thinking Friday-to-Sunday, and do you want to fly into Madison itself or consider Milwaukee if the flights are much easier?
Friday to Sunday. I’m open to Milwaukee, but I don’t want the travel logistics to eat the whole weekend. It’s me and my spouse, no kids.

Here’s the practical shortlist. First: Denver to Madison on Friday afternoon with one connection, arriving early evening. It costs more than the cheapest path but keeps you close to the event and avoids a late-night drive. Second: nonstop Denver to Milwaukee, then rent a car and drive about 80 to 90 minutes to Madison. Lower airfare, but you add the rental counter and highway time. Third: the cheap later itinerary into Madison, but it lands close to midnight, so it only works if Friday dinner definitely disappears and you’re okay arriving tired.
If there is a Friday dinner, we would need to be there by about 7. If there is no Friday dinner, arriving at 8 or 9 is fine. What are the rough flight times?

The Madison one-stop I’d keep on the list leaves Denver early afternoon, connects for about an hour, and gets into Madison around 6:40 to 7:00. That could still make a 7:30-ish casual dinner, but not a formal 7:00 seating. The Milwaukee nonstop arrives around 4:00 to 4:30; after rental pickup and the drive, you’re also realistically in Madison around 6:30. The cheap Madison itinerary leaves after work and arrives around 11:30, so it’s the clear backup only.
How bad is that Milwaukee drive on a Friday?

Not terrible, but it’s not invisible. Budget 20 to 30 minutes for the rental counter, then 90 minutes to Madison if traffic behaves. If the flight is delayed or weather is messy, it becomes the more annoying option even though the flight itself is nonstop.
So Madison airport is simpler, Milwaukee is cheaper but not necessarily faster door to door.

Exactly. If the Madison fare is within about $125 to $150 per person of Milwaukee, I’d lean Madison for this weekend. Once you add rental cost, fuel, parking, and the hassle factor, Milwaukee only wins if the airfare gap is large or the Madison connection is ugly.
Hotels are probably the harder part. We’ll mostly be with family, so I don’t need a resort, but I also don’t want a sad graduation-weekend motel.

Three areas make sense. Campus area: best for walking to graduation and meeting relatives, but rates are higher and amenities are thin. West side: better value, easier parking, more suite-style properties, but you’ll drive to campus. Lakeside downtown: nicest room experience, some balcony rooms, but pricier and less useful if you’re barely in the room.
Give me actual candidates.

Ranked for this trip: 1. West-side suite property, about 15 to 20 minutes from campus, around a 4.3 to 4.4 guest rating, free parking, breakfast, pool, hot tub, and fitness room. Best balance if you rent a car. 2. Campus-area hotel, roughly 4.4 rating, great location for the ceremony, but limited fitness access and no real pool/hot tub setup; parking may be valet or extra. 3. Lakeside boutique, about 4.5 rating with balcony-room categories, but higher nightly rates and no pool, so it’s more of a splurge than a practical family-weekend choice.
The balcony sounds nice, but if we’re with family all day it may be wasted. I do like having a pool or hot tub if we’re out on our feet.

Then the west-side suite option is the one to protect now, especially if it has a refundable rate. It gives you recovery amenities and parking without paying downtown graduation pricing. If the family later confirms everything is campus-based and no one can help with rides, we can revisit campus, but rooms may tighten.
Would we need a rental car if we stay west side?

Yes, I’d plan on a small rental car for the west side. Rideshares can work, but graduation traffic and scattered family events make a car easier. If you stay campus or lakeside, you could skip the rental and rideshare from MSN, but then you’re paying more for location.
What should I hold before the family decides dinner versus brunch?

Hold a refundable west-side king or suite for Friday and Saturday nights first. For flights, watch the Friday afternoon Madison one-stop and the Milwaukee nonstop, but don’t commit to the late cheap flight unless Friday is definitely free. Ask the family two questions: is Friday dinner real, and is Sunday brunch before noon or later? Those answers decide whether you need the earlier Friday arrival and whether a mid-afternoon Sunday return is safer than a morning flight.

messages.content: Madison update: family dinner is not happening Friday. The main gathering is Saturday evening after the ceremony, and Sunday is just informal goodbyes. Can we pick the flights and hotel now?

Yes. That makes the Friday afternoon Denver-to-Madison one-stop the best fit. It is now only a little more than Milwaukee once you count the rental time, fuel, and parking, and it avoids the late cheap itinerary that gets you in close to midnight.
Let’s do Madison airport unless the connection is too tight.

Use the afternoon one-stop with the roughly hour-plus connection, not the tighter version. It should get you to Madison early evening Friday, which is fine now that there’s no dinner. For Sunday, take the early-to-mid afternoon return so you can do the informal family goodbye without rushing out at breakfast.
What happened with the hotels?

The campus hotel lost Saturday availability, so I’d drop it. The lakeside balcony room is still attractive, but it’s hard to justify for a family-focused weekend. Book the west-side suite property with the king room: parking included, pool, hot tub, fitness access, and a better rate.
Do we definitely need a car with that hotel?

Yes, reserve a small car at Madison airport from Friday evening to Sunday afternoon. No SUV needed. It gives you easy campus access, family-event flexibility, and avoids relying on rideshares during graduation traffic.
Okay, book that plan. What notes should I add before I hit purchase?

Add these notes: choose a window seat for you with your spouse next to you if paired seats are open; avoid splitting up just to get a better row. For the hotel, request a quiet king room away from elevators and note Friday evening arrival. For the family, say you’ll land Friday early evening, handle dinner on your own, be ready for the Saturday ceremony and evening gathering, and plan a Sunday afternoon departure. Before final purchase, confirm the hotel cancellation deadline and that the rental car pickup matches the flight arrival.
